cards.hypothesis: Inter-subject variability in autonomic nervous system regulation causes conformal prediction sets to undercover for subjects with high heart rate variability during calibration but low variability during deployment.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Subjects with high baseline heart rate variability (HRV) exhibit wider prediction intervals during calibration; when deployed on low-HRV segments (e.g., during stress), the fixed quantile threshold yields intervals too narrow for the reduced variability, causing undercoverage.
cards.causal_path: High baseline HRV (RMSSD > 50ms) → wider calibration residuals → larger conformal quantile → deployment on low-HRV segments (RMSSD < 20ms) → residual distribution contraction → fixed quantile exceeds true variability → coverage drop
control_variables: stratify calibration by baseline HRV tertiles
match deployment segments to calibration HRV range
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability stems from sensor noise floor differences across recording sessions, not physiological variability.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage drops correlate with sensor signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) changes, not HRV changes; subjects with stable SNR maintain coverage regardless of HRV shift.
cards.distinguishing_test: Regress coverage error against both ΔRMSSD and ΔSNR; HRV mechanism predicts significant ΔRMSSD coefficient (p<0.01) while SNR coefficient is non-significant.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Prior work shows HRV changes of 30ms RMSSD alter prediction interval widths by 15-25% in ECG-derived respiration; pilot data from 20 subjects would estimate exact magnitude.
minimum_data_needed: Continuous ECG with R-peak annotations for ≥50 subjects
Simultaneous reference respiration (impedance or belt) for ground truth
Segment-level HRV metrics (RMSSD, SDNN) per 5-min window
Conformal prediction residuals per segment from a trained model
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage error (nominal - empirical) increases by ≥5 percentage points when deployment segment RMSSD is >30ms lower than calibration median RMSSD.
cards.failure_condition: Coverage error shows no correlation with ΔRMSSD (Spearman ρ < 0.1, p > 0.2) across segments.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Mixed-effects logistic regression: coverage_indicator ~ ΔRMSSD + (1|subject) + SNR + motion_artifact_flag; test ΔRMSSD coefficient ≠ 0 with α=0.01.
cards.falsification_test: Artificially subsample high-HRV calibration data to match low-HRV deployment variability; if coverage stabilizes, HRV mechanism is confirmed; if coverage remains unstable, mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Electrode-skin impedance drift during long recordings alters ECG morphology non-uniformly across leads, violating exchangeability between calibration and deployment segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Impedance increases >5 kΩ over 2+ hours attenuate high-frequency ECG components (QRS slope, T-wave amplitude) differentially across leads; conformal scores calibrated on low-impedance segments misestimate uncertainty for high-impedance segments.
cards.causal_path: Recording duration >2hr → electrode gel drying → impedance rise >5kΩ (measured at 10Hz) → QRS max dV/dt attenuation >20% in affected leads → residual distribution shift → conformal quantile miscalibration → coverage instability
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is caused by physiological non-stationarity (e.g., circadian QT interval changes), not electrode degradation.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage drops correlate with time-of-day and QT interval changes, not impedance; impedance-corrected features show same instability.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage error in segments matched for time-of-day but differing in impedance; impedance mechanism predicts significant impedance effect (p<0.01) after controlling for time-of-day.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Literature reports 30-50% QRS amplitude attenuation at 10kΩ vs 1kΩ; conformal scores scale with feature magnitude, so 20%+ coverage shifts expected. Pilot impedance-tracking data from 10 long recordings would quantify.
minimum_data_needed: Continuous electrode impedance measurements (10Hz) synchronized with ECG
Multi-lead ECG (≥3 leads) with fiducial point annotations
Segment-level conformal scores and coverage outcomes
Skin preparation protocol metadata per session
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with mean impedance >8kΩ show ≥10 percentage points lower coverage than segments <3kΩ, after controlling for time-of-day and subject.
cards.failure_condition: Impedance explains <2% of coverage error variance in hierarchical model (marginal R² < 0.02).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_error ~ mean_impedance + time_of_day + (1|subject) + (1|session); likelihood ratio test for impedance term.
cards.falsification_test: Apply impedance normalization (amplitude scaling per lead by 1kΩ/reference_impedance) to all segments; if coverage instability persists identically, impedance mechanism is falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Motion artifact bursts during specific activities (e.g., walking, eating) create heteroscedastic residuals that violate the i.i.d. assumption of split conformal prediction.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Transient motion artifacts (accelerometer magnitude >0.5g) induce non-Gaussian residual tails during calibration; the conformal quantile adapts to these heavy tails, but deployment segments without artifacts receive over-wide intervals (overcoverage), while artifact-heavy deployment segments still undercover due to distribution shift.
cards.causal_path: Activity type → accelerometer_RMS >0.5g → motion artifact contamination → residual kurtosis >10 in calibration → inflated conformal quantile → deployment on clean segments → overcoverage; deployment on artifact segments → residual distribution mismatch → undercoverage
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage variation reflects true physiological signal complexity changes during activities, not artifacts.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage correlates with physiological complexity metrics (sample entropy, Lempel-Ziv) not accelerometer magnitude; artifact-rejected data shows same pattern.
cards.distinguishing_test: Train conformal predictor on artifact-rejected calibration data only; artifact mechanism predicts coverage stabilizes (error <2%), rival predicts instability persists.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Studies show motion artifacts increase residual variance 3-5x; conformal quantile at 90% coverage scales with √variance, so 70-120% interval width changes expected. Need artifact-labeled data from 30+ subjects across activities.
minimum_data_needed: Triaxial accelerometer synchronized with physiological signals
Manual or validated automatic artifact labels per segment
Conformal residuals per segment from base predictor
Activity labels (sit, stand, walk, eat, sleep) per segment
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage error standard deviation across activity types exceeds 8 percentage points when calibration includes artifacts, but drops below 3 points when calibration uses artifact-rejected data only.
cards.failure_condition: Artifact-rejected calibration yields coverage error SD >5 percentage points across activities.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Levene's test for equality of coverage error variance across activity types between full vs artifact-rejected calibration; F-test with α=0.01.
cards.falsification_test: Inject synthetic motion artifacts (scaled real artifact templates) into clean deployment segments at varying intensities; if coverage error tracks injected artifact intensity (R²>0.7), mechanism confirmed; if flat, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Circadian-driven changes in QT interval and T-wave morphology cause systematic residual distribution shifts between morning and night segments that conformal prediction cannot adapt to without retraining.
cards.proposed_mechanism: QT interval prolongs by 30-50ms at night due to autonomic shift; model trained on mixed-day data learns average morphology; conformal scores calibrated on day segments underestimate night residuals (undercoverage), while night-calibrated scores overestimate day residuals (overcoverage).
cards.causal_path: Circadian phase (melatonin onset) → autonomic balance shift → QT_interval prolongation >30ms + T_wave_amplitude reduction >15% → model residual mean shift + variance change → fixed conformal quantile miscalibration → coverage divergence by time-of-day
control_variables: stratify calibration by circadian phase (dim-light melatonin onset)
separate conformal predictors per circadian bin
cards.rival_explanation: Time-of-day coverage differences reflect behavioral state (sleep vs wake) not circadian biology; controlling for activity eliminates the effect.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage stabilizes when conditioning on activity/posture (supine vs upright) regardless of clock time; circadian phase adds no explanatory power.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compare nested models: coverage_error ~ activity + posture vs coverage_error ~ activity + posture + circadian_phase; circadian mechanism predicts significant circadian_phase term (p<0.01).
cards.effect_size_rationale: QT circadian amplitude ~30-50ms; typical QT prediction RMSE ~15ms; residual distribution shift of 2-3 RMSE units could cause 10-15% coverage swings. Need 24-hr recordings with melatonin assays from 20+ subjects.
minimum_data_needed: 24+ hour continuous ECG with fiducials
Dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) assay or validated proxy per subject
Posture/activity labels per segment
Conformal residuals and coverage per segment
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage error differs by ≥8 percentage points between circadian phases (biological night vs day) after controlling for posture and activity.
cards.failure_condition: Circadian phase coefficient non-significant (p>0.05) in mixed model with activity/posture covariates.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Generalized additive mixed model: coverage_indicator ~ s(circadian_phase) + activity + posture + (1|subject); test smooth term significance via approximate p-value.
cards.falsification_test: Retrain base model and conformal predictor separately on biological day vs night data; if segment-specific predictors eliminate coverage gap, mechanism confirmed; if gap persists, mechanism falsified (points to unmeasured confounder).

cards.hypothesis: Inconsistent R-peak annotation quality across segments (due to automated algorithm failures on low-SNR regions) introduces label noise that biases conformal score distributions.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Automated R-peak detectors miss beats or insert false positives in low-SNR segments (SNR < 10dB); this creates erroneous RR intervals used as targets, inflating residuals non-randomly; conformal quantile absorbs this noise, but deployment on clean segments yields overcoverage while noisy segments still undercover.
cards.causal_path: Segment SNR <10dB → R-peak detection F1 <0.9 → RR_interval_error >50ms → residual inflation → calibration quantile expansion → deployment on high-SNR segments → overcoverage; deployment on low-SNR → residual distribution mismatch → undercoverage
control_variables: manual R-peak verification on calibration set
use detector confidence scores as weights
exclude segments with F1<0.95 from calibration
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability reflects true physiological RR interval variability increases in low-SNR segments (which correlate with stress/activity), not annotation errors.
cards.rival_prediction: Manual verification of R-peaks in low-SNR segments shows high physiological variability (SDNN >100ms) not annotation errors; coverage error correlates with true SDNN not F1 score.
cards.distinguishing_test: Compute coverage error vs both segment_SNR and manually_verified_SDNN; annotation mechanism predicts SNR/F1 significant (p<0.01) while SDNN non-significant after controlling for SNR.
cards.effect_size_rationale: R-peak errors of 50ms on 800ms RR intervals = 6% relative error; conformal scores directly use these errors; pilot data shows 15-25% coverage swings with detector quality. Need 100+ segments with manual R-peak ground truth.
minimum_data_needed: ECG with manual R-peak annotations (gold standard) for ≥100 segments
Automated R-peak detector outputs per segment
Segment-level SNR estimates
Conformal residuals and coverage per segment
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with automated R-peak F1 <0.9 show ≥12 percentage points coverage error vs segments with F1 >0.98, after controlling for true HRV.
cards.failure_condition: Manual R-peak verification reveals annotation error rate <2% in all segments, yet coverage instability persists.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Quantile regression: coverage_error ~ R_peak_F1 + true_SDNN + SNR + (1|subject); test F1 coefficient at τ=0.5 and τ=0.9.
cards.falsification_test: Replace automated R-peaks with manual annotations for all segments; retrain conformal predictor; if coverage stabilizes (error SD <3%), mechanism confirmed; if instability remains, mechanism falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Improper stratification of calibration data by physiological state (e.g., stress vs rest) causes conformal quantiles to reflect mixture distributions, failing to cover any single state adequately.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Calibration set mixes high-stress (sympathetic dominant) and low-stress (parasympathetic dominant) segments with different residual variances; the pooled conformal quantile covers the mixture but undercovers high-variance states and overcovers low-variance states.
cards.causal_path: Unstratified calibration → mixture of high-stress (LF/HF >3) and low-stress (LF/HF <1) segments → bimodal residual distribution → single quantile at 90th percentile of mixture → deployment on pure high-stress → undercoverage; deployment on pure low-stress → overcoverage
control_variables: ensure calibration set state distribution matches deployment
include LF/HF as covariate in base model
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage differences reflect model misspecification (nonlinear HRV effects) not calibration stratification; a better base model would eliminate the need for stratification.
cards.rival_prediction: Retraining base model with LF/HF interaction terms equalizes residual variance across states; pooled conformal then achieves stable coverage without stratification.
cards.distinguishing_test: Train base model with LF/HF × feature interactions; compare coverage stability of pooled conformal on interaction-model residuals vs stratified conformal on original residuals; rival predicts interaction-model + pooled works as well as stratified.
cards.effect_size_rationale: LF/HF ratio varies 10-100x across states; residual variance scales with sympathetic tone; pilot data from stress protocols shows 2-3x residual variance ratio. Need labeled stress/rest segments from 30+ subjects.
minimum_data_needed: ECG with HRV spectral analysis (LF, HF power) per segment
Validated stress/rest labels (e.g., via protocol or self-report)
Conformal residuals per segment from base model
Deployment segments with known physiological state
cards.testable_prediction: Pooled conformal coverage error SD across LF/HF tertiles ≥10 percentage points; state-stratified conformal reduces SD to ≤3 points.
cards.failure_condition: State-stratified conformal shows coverage error SD >5 percentage points across states.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Brown-Forsythe test for equality of coverage error variances across LF/HF tertiles between pooled vs stratified conformal; α=0.01.
cards.falsification_test: Construct calibration set with perfectly balanced LF/HF distribution matching deployment; if coverage instability persists, stratification mechanism falsified (points to within-state non-stationarity).

cards.hypothesis: Medication-induced changes in cardiac electrophysiology (e.g., beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers) create subpopulations with distinct residual distributions that violate exchangeability when pooled.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Beta-blockers reduce heart rate and increase HRV, altering ECG morphology (prolonged PR, widened QRS); model trained on mixed medicated/unmedicated data learns compromised representations; conformal scores from medicated subjects have systematically lower variance, causing overcoverage for them and undercoverage for unmedicated when pooled.
cards.causal_path: Beta_blocker_use → HR_increase >15bpm + PR_prolongation >20ms + HRV_increase >30% → residual_distribution_shift (mean -15%, std -25%) → pooled conformal quantile → medicated deployment → overcoverage; unmedicated deployment → undercoverage
control_variables: separate conformal predictors per medication status
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage differences reflect disease severity (indication bias), not medication effect; sicker patients have more variable physiology regardless of meds.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage error correlates with disease severity score (e.g., CHA2DS2-VASc) not medication status; medication-stratified conformal shows same instability within severity strata.
cards.distinguishing_test: Propensity-score match medicated/unmedicated subjects on severity; compare coverage error between matched pairs; medication mechanism predicts significant pair difference (p<0.01), rival predicts none.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Beta-blockers reduce HR by 15-25bpm and increase RMSSD by 20-40ms; prior conformal work shows 10-15% coverage shifts per 10bpm HR change. Need medicated/unmedicated cohorts with ECG and medication records (n≥50 each).
minimum_data_needed: ECG with medication records (dose, class, timing)
Heart rate, PR interval, HRV metrics per segment
Disease severity scores (CHA2DS2-VASc or similar)
Conformal residuals and coverage per segment
cards.testable_prediction: Medicated subjects show ≥7 percentage points higher coverage than unmedicated at nominal 90% level when using pooled conformal; medication-stratified conformal eliminates this gap.
cards.failure_condition: Propensity-matched pairs show coverage difference <2 percentage points (95% CI includes 0).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Paired t-test on coverage error between propensity-matched medicated/unmedicated pairs; equivalence test (TOST) with bounds ±3%.
cards.falsification_test: Train base model with medication status as input feature + interaction terms; apply pooled conformal; if coverage gap closes, medication effect was via model misspecification not exchangeability violation (falsifies pure exchangeability mechanism).

cards.hypothesis: Non-stationary baseline wander (respiratory, motion-induced) with time-varying amplitude and frequency violates the conformal assumption of exchangeable residuals across segments.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Baseline wander amplitude modulates with respiration depth and body position; segments with high wander amplitude (>0.5mV) distort ECG features (ST segment, T wave) causing residual inflation; conformal quantile calibrated on mixed-wander data miscalibrates for extreme-wander segments.
cards.causal_path: Respiration_depth >1L tidal volume OR supine→standing transition → baseline_wander_amplitude >0.5mV (0.05-0.5Hz) → ST_segment_distortion >0.1mV → feature_extraction_error → residual_inflation → conformal_quantile_mismatch → coverage_instability
control_variables: include wander amplitude as model feature
cards.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is driven by respiration-induced heart rate variability (RSA), not baseline wander; wander is a correlate not cause.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage error correlates with RSA magnitude (HF power) not wander amplitude; wander-corrected ECG shows same coverage pattern.
cards.distinguishing_test: Apply high-pass filter at 0.5Hz (removes wander) vs 0.05Hz (preserves wander) to same data; wander mechanism predicts coverage stabilizes with 0.5Hz filter; RSA mechanism predicts no change.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Baseline wander typically <0.3mV in controlled settings but can reach 1mV during deep breathing/motion; feature distortion ~0.1mV; expected coverage shift 3-8%. Need simultaneous ECG, respiration belt, and posture data from 25+ subjects.
minimum_data_needed: ECG with simultaneous respiration belt (tidal volume estimate)
Posture labels per segment
Baseline wander amplitude per segment (0.05-0.5Hz bandpower)
Conformal residuals and coverage per segment
cards.testable_prediction: Segments with wander amplitude >0.5mV show ≥5 percentage points lower coverage than segments <0.1mV when using 0.05Hz high-pass; difference <2 points with 0.5Hz high-pass.
cards.failure_condition: High-pass filter at 0.5Hz does not reduce coverage error SD across wander amplitude bins (Levene's test p>0.05).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Two-way ANOVA: coverage_error ~ filter_cutoff (0.05 vs 0.5Hz) × wander_bin (low/med/high) + (1|subject); test interaction term.
cards.falsification_test: Synthesize baseline wander (sinusoids 0.1-0.3Hz, amplitude 0-1mV) added to clean ECG; measure coverage error vs injected amplitude; if error tracks amplitude (R²>0.6), mechanism confirmed; if flat, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Finite-sample conformal quantile estimation error is amplified in short physiological segments (<30 beats) due to high residual quantile variance, causing unstable coverage segment-to-segment.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Short segments (e.g., 30-second windows at 60bpm = 30 beats) yield noisy empirical quantiles; the 90th percentile of 30 residuals has standard error ~√(0.9×0.1/30) ≈ 5.5% of residual scale; this sampling variability dominates coverage fluctuations, not true distribution shifts.
cards.causal_path: Segment_duration <30s → n_beats <30 → conformal_quantile_SE >5% of residual_scale → coverage_indicator variance dominated by quantile_estimation_error → apparent coverage instability across segments even under perfect exchangeability
control_variables: report coverage with binomial confidence intervals
cards.rival_explanation: Observed coverage instability reflects true physiological non-stationarity at short timescales, not quantile estimation error.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage instability persists even with 500-beat segments; instability correlates with physiological complexity metrics, not 1/√n_beats.
cards.distinguishing_test: Plot coverage error variance vs 1/n_beats across segment lengths; quantile-error mechanism predicts linear relationship (R²>0.7); rival predicts flat or physiological-correlate relationship.
cards.effect_size_rationale: Binomial quantile SE formula gives exact expectation: for n=30, 90% quantile SE ≈ 0.055 in probability units; translates to ~5-10% coverage SD. Purely statistical, no pilot data needed for estimate.
minimum_data_needed: Conformal scores from base model on long recordings
Ability to subsample segments at varying beat counts (10, 30, 100, 300, 1000)
Ground truth coverage per segment length via repeated sampling
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage error standard deviation scales as 1/√n_beats (R²>0.8) for n_beats <100; plateaus for n_beats >300.
cards.failure_condition: Coverage error SD shows no correlation with 1/√n_beats (Spearman ρ < 0.2, p > 0.2).
cards.statistical_test_plan: Weighted least squares: log(coverage_error_SD) ~ log(n_beats) + heart_rate + (1|subject); test slope = -0.5.
cards.falsification_test: Use smoothed conformal prediction (kernel density estimation of scores with bandwidth selected by cross-validation) on short segments; if coverage instability disappears, quantile estimation mechanism confirmed; if persists, falsified.

cards.hypothesis: Environmental temperature shifts alter peripheral vasoconstriction and skin conductance, changing PPG/ECG signal morphology and noise characteristics in a way that breaks conformal exchangeability.
cards.proposed_mechanism: Ambient temperature drops >5°C cause peripheral vasoconstriction, reducing PPG amplitude by 30-50% and increasing motion artifact susceptibility; ECG contact impedance rises; model trained at 22°C misestimates uncertainty at 15°C; conformal quantile calibrated at one temperature fails at another.
cards.causal_path: Ambient_temp_drop >5°C → cutaneous_vasoconstriction → PPG_AC_amplitude ↓30-50% + ECG_impedance ↑40% → SNR ↓6dB + morphology_change → residual_distribution_shift → fixed_conformal_quantile_mismatch → coverage_drop
cards.rival_explanation: Temperature effects are mediated entirely by heart rate changes (thermoregulatory tachycardia/bradycardia); controlling for HR eliminates temperature effect.
cards.rival_prediction: Coverage error correlates with HR not temperature; temperature-stratified conformal shows same instability within HR-matched bins.
cards.distinguishing_test: Mixed model: coverage_error ~ temperature + heart_rate + (1|subject); temperature mechanism predicts significant temperature coefficient (p<0.01) after HR adjustment.
cards.effect_size_rationale: PPG amplitude changes ~2%/°C; 5°C drop = 10% amplitude change; SNR change ~1-2dB; expected coverage shift 2-5%. Need controlled temperature chamber data or seasonal outdoor data with temp logs from 20+ subjects.
minimum_data_needed: Continuous ambient temperature logging synchronized with physiological signals
PPG and ECG with amplitude/impedance metrics per segment
Heart rate per segment
Conformal residuals and coverage per segment
cards.testable_prediction: Coverage error decreases by ≥3 percentage points per 5°C temperature drop after controlling for heart rate; temperature-stratified conformal reduces error SD by ≥40%.
cards.failure_condition: Temperature coefficient non-significant (p>0.05) in model with HR covariate; temperature-stratified conformal shows no improvement.
cards.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed model: coverage_error ~ ambient_temp + heart_rate + (1|subject) + (1|session); Wald test for temperature coefficient.
cards.falsification_test: Normalize PPG amplitude by its segment-wise median (removing vasoconstriction effect) and re-extract features; retrain conformal predictor; if coverage stabilizes across temperatures, mechanism confirmed; if instability persists, mechanism falsified (points to unmeasured temperature effect).
